title: Repair or recalibration: the paired Terminal-Bench 3.0 to 4.0 re-run under one pinned harness, with a resources-only hybrid arm on the 19 fixed tasks
statement: Step 0 (data gate, $0, 2 days): pull Harbor Hub revisions 1 (tag 3.0.0) and 4 (tag 4.0.0) of terminal-bench/terminal-bench, diff every task directory to label the kept, removed and repaired sets by which files changed (instruction, environment, verifier, or resource settings only), count the 3.0 tasks, confirm that the pinned harness runs the 3.0.0 revision on one task, price the two models and the sandbox hours from the providers' pages, and open one 4.0 leaderboard job page to record whether per-trial, per-task outcomes with end reasons are exposed. Step 1 (within-4.0 ordering test, $0, 2 days, conditional on step 0's job-page check): on the 35-entry by 66-task by 5-trial matrix, the Spearman correlation between entry orderings on the 19 repaired tasks and on the 47 untouched tasks, against a difficulty-matched random-subset null (2609.00482's matched-random subtests, strata by 4.0 pass rate). Step 2 (paired re-run, at most $1.5k, 0 to 20 GPU-hours, 10 days): two open-weight models under one harness pinned by commit (mini-SWE-agent, which runs on the 4.0 board) at a stated temperature, 3 trials per cell, on every 3.0.0 task (the removed tasks included, for the composition term), every 4.0.0 task, and a hybrid arm of the 19 repaired tasks' 3.0.0 content under 4.0.0 resource settings, every trial logged with its end reason (pass, fail, agent timeout, out-of-memory or resource kill, output-token-exceeded, refusal, infrastructure error); readouts are the repair effect at fixed resources $\delta^{\ast}$, the recalibration effect on repaired tasks $\gamma_R$ and on untouched tasks $\bar\Delta_U$, the difference-in-differences $\delta$, the kept-task delta, the composition term, the repair share $\hat\pi$ with a task-cluster bootstrap, and a double-verifier re-grade on the repaired tasks whose only change is the verifier.
claim: On Terminal-Bench 3.0 to 4.0, with the model fixed and the harness pinned, the 19 repaired tasks move by more than 0.15 pass-rate points beyond the recalibration lift measured on the 47 untouched tasks (so that the repair channel carries more than half of the kept-task delta whenever that lift is at most 0.043 points), and the entry ordering on the repaired tasks departs from the ordering on the untouched tasks beyond a difficulty-matched random-subset ceiling.
trick: Run the same model through the same harness on both versions of the benchmark, and on the fixed tasks once more with only the new resource limits, so the score change splits into what the repairs did, what the new limits did, and what was dice.
equations: E1, per-cell pass rate: $p_{t,m}(c, r) = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^{k} y_{t,m,j}(c, r)$, where $t$ is a task, $m$ a model ($M = 2$), $c \in \{3, 4\}$ the task content (instruction, environment, verifier) of revision 3.0.0 or 4.0.0, $r \in \{3, 4\}$ the resource settings (agent timeout, CPU, memory) of that revision, $j$ the trial, $k = 3$ trials per cell, and $y \in \{0, 1\}$ the verifier's outcome. Arms run: $(3,3)$ on all 3.0.0 tasks, $(4,4)$ on all 4.0.0 tasks, $(3,4)$ on the repaired set only.

E2, per-task version delta and set means: $\Delta_t = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m}\big[p_{t,m}(4,4) - p_{t,m}(3,3)\big]$ for $t \in R \cup U$; $\bar\Delta_R = \frac{1}{n_R}\sum_{t \in R}\Delta_t$, $\bar\Delta_U = \frac{1}{n_U}\sum_{t \in U}\Delta_t$, with $R$ the repaired set ($n_R = 19$) and $U$ the untouched set ($n_U = 47$) as labelled by the step-0 diff.

E3, repair effect at fixed resources (primary estimand) and recalibration effect on the repaired tasks: $\delta^{\ast} = \frac{1}{n_R}\sum_{t \in R}\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m}\big[p_{t,m}(4,4) - p_{t,m}(3,4)\big]$, $\gamma_R = \frac{1}{n_R}\sum_{t \in R}\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m}\big[p_{t,m}(3,4) - p_{t,m}(3,3)\big]$, so that $\bar\Delta_R = \delta^{\ast} + \gamma_R$ exactly; the parallel-trends check is $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$ (zero when the recalibration lifts repaired and untouched tasks alike).

E4, difference-in-differences (the estimate a lab with only both-version logs can form): $\delta = \bar\Delta_R - \bar\Delta_U = \delta^{\ast} + (\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U)$; $\delta$ equals $\delta^{\ast}$ only under parallel trends, and the hybrid arm measures the gap instead of assuming it away.

E5, kept-task delta, repair share and the half line: $\Delta_{\mathrm{kept}} = \frac{n_R\bar\Delta_R + n_U\bar\Delta_U}{n_R + n_U}$ (uniform task weights, as on the board); $\hat\pi = \frac{n_R\,\delta^{\ast}}{n_R\bar\Delta_R + n_U\bar\Delta_U}$ (and $\hat\pi_{\mathrm{DiD}}$ with $\delta$ in place of $\delta^{\ast}$); $\hat\pi > \tfrac{1}{2} \iff \delta^{\ast} > \gamma_R + \tfrac{n_U}{n_R}\,\bar\Delta_U$, which under parallel trends ($\gamma_R = \bar\Delta_U$) reads $\delta^{\ast} > \tfrac{n_R + n_U}{n_R}\,\bar\Delta_U = 3.47\,\bar\Delta_U$ (equivalently $\bar\Delta_R > \tfrac{2n_R + n_U}{n_R}\,\bar\Delta_U = 4.47\,\bar\Delta_U$), so the 0.15-point kill line and the 0.5 share line coincide at $\bar\Delta_U = 0.15 / 3.47 = 0.043$. The share is read only when $\Delta_{\mathrm{kept}}$'s interval excludes zero (a ratio with a denominator inside its own noise is undefined, not small).

E6, composition term, exact: $\bar p^{(4,4)}_{\mathrm{kept}} - \bar p^{(3,3)}_{\mathrm{all}} = \Delta_{\mathrm{kept}} + \Delta_{\mathrm{comp}}$ with $\Delta_{\mathrm{comp}} = \frac{n_X}{n_R + n_U + n_X}\big(\bar p^{(3,3)}_{\mathrm{kept}} - \bar p^{(3,3)}_{X}\big)$, $X$ the removed set ($n_X = 8$ if the diff confirms the release note) and $\bar p^{(3,3)}_{X}$ its mean 3.0 pass rate for the same models; reported beside the share, never inside it.

E7, verifier-only re-grade: for $t \in R_V \subseteq R$ (tasks whose diff touches only the verifier), $\Delta^{\mathrm{ver}}_t = \frac{1}{kM}\sum_{m, j}\big[V^{4}_t(\omega_{t,m,j}) - V^{3}_t(\omega_{t,m,j})\big]$, where $\omega_{t,m,j}$ is the end state of trial $j$ in the $(4,4)$ arm and $V^{v}_t$ the version-$v$ verifier run on that same end state (both verifiers run at the end of each trial, no extra API cost); for $t \in R_V$ the difference $\delta^{\ast}_t - \Delta^{\mathrm{ver}}_t$ is expected to sit inside run noise, which checks the arm.

E8, task-cluster bootstrap: resample the $n_R$ repaired tasks with replacement and the $n_U$ untouched tasks with replacement, separately (stratified), recompute every statistic in E2 to E6, $B = 2000$ draws, 95% percentile intervals; models are a fixed factor (not resampled) and each model's estimates are reported beside the pooled ones; trials inside a task are never resampled on their own (the task is the cluster).

E9, ordering test (step 1): $q_{e,t} = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{j=1}^{5} y_{e,t,j}$ for board entry $e$ ($E = 35$) and task $t$; $s_e(S) = \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{t \in S} q_{e,t}$; $\rho_{RU} = \rho_s\big(s_{\cdot}(R), s_{\cdot}(U)\big)$, Spearman over entries. Difficulty-matched random-subset null: $d_t = \frac{1}{E}\sum_e q_{e,t}$; strata $h = 1, \ldots, 4$ by quartile of $d_t$ over the 66 tasks; $n_{R,h}$ the number of repaired tasks in stratum $h$; for $b = 1, \ldots, B$ draw $S^{(b)}$ with $n_{R,h}$ tasks from each stratum and $\bar S^{(b)}$ its complement, $\rho^{(b)} = \rho_s\big(s_{\cdot}(S^{(b)}), s_{\cdot}(\bar S^{(b)})\big)$; the ceiling $c_{0.05}$ is the 5th percentile of $\{\rho^{(b)}\}$, and the clause holds if $\rho_{RU} < c_{0.05}$. The unstratified 19-of-66 null is reported beside it so the composition term's size is visible; a secondary run collapses the 35 entries to one row per model (23 models, the highest-effort row) because effort levels of one model are not independent orderings.
why_now: Terminal-Bench 4.0: the 4-0-0 leaderboard registry on the Harbor Hub was created 2026-08-27T18:30Z (the release note, dated 2026-08-28 in the pressure record, is undated on the page) and its payload was last updated 2026-10-23T00:29Z (35 entries, every row 330 trials, fetched 2026-11-02); the Hub keeps revision 1 (tag 3.0.0) and revision 4 (tag 4.0.0) addressable under one CLI (page fetched 2026-11-02), so both versions run as shipped; the release note says 'These represent breaking changes that require re-running trials', names 19 fixed and 8 removed tasks and a flat 8-hour timeout, and points to 'the GitHub release and each individual task's README changelog' for the per-task diff; the recalibration followed a published methodology (Anthropic, 'Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals', 2026-02-05: +6 points from resource headroom on Terminal-Bench 2.0, infra errors 5.8% to 0.5%), which makes the recalibration channel a named, measured quantity for the first time; 2609.00482 (2026-08-31) supplied the matched-random subtest null and 2610.11678 (2026-10-08) the identical-rerun flip band (15-36%). Before 4.0 no agent benchmark had two addressable revisions with a per-task changelog and a full re-run requirement on every task; the 5.0 milestone ('new tasks') is live, so the owner is the race.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0, data gate ($0, 2 days; see data_gate). Step 1, ordering ($0, 2 days, only if the job pages expose per-task outcomes): compute $\rho_{RU}$ and the difficulty-matched null (E9) on the 35 x 66 x 5 matrix; secondary on one row per model. Step 2, re-run (10 days): harness mini-SWE-agent at one commit, temperature set explicitly in the harness config and reported (the board's own mini-SWE-agent rows are the reference configuration); model A = GLM-5.3-Flash (on the 4.0 board under Claude Code at 35.76% accuracy, $118.74 for 330 trials, 8.8M tokens per trial), model B = the cheapest open-weight model whose blended price at step 0 keeps the total at or under $1.5k (the rule below); cells: $(3,3)$ on all 3.0.0 tasks (74 if the diff confirms 66 kept + 8 removed), $(4,4)$ on all 66 4.0.0 tasks, $(3,4)$ on the 19 repaired tasks; $k = 3$ trials per cell; 2 x 3 x (74 + 66 + 19) = 954 trials; the six cells of a task are run in one time window with arms alternating, so wall-clock drift (API latency, host load) enters every arm alike; every trial logs its end reason and duration; both verifiers run at the end of each $(4,4)$ trial on tasks in $R_V$ (E7). Readouts: E2 to E8 pooled and per model; $\bar\Delta_U$ with and without trials that ended by timeout, resource kill or output-token-exceeded; per-stratum results by 4.0 difficulty quartile. Budget arithmetic: dollars $= 954 \times \bar T \times \bar c$, with $\bar T$ the tokens per trial under mini-SWE-agent (the 4.0 board's two mini-SWE-agent rows: 11.14B/330 = 34M and 17.19B/330 = 52M; 40M assumed) and $\bar c$ the mean blended price per million tokens of the two models; at GLM-5.3-Flash's board-derived rate ($118.74 / 2.92B = \$0.041$ per million) the full design for both models costs about $1.56k, so model B must price at or under about $0.04 per million blended for the full design; otherwise model B runs the reduced set (19 repaired x 2 versions + 19 difficulty-matched untouched x 2 versions + 19 hybrid = 95 cells, 285 trials) and the pooled $\bar\Delta_U$ keeps model A's 47 tasks; if no open-weight model B fits even the reduced set, the design runs with $M = 1$ and the stated power loss (kill power 0.62 to 0.36). Not chosen and why: GLM-5.3 and Qwen3.8-Max-0902 are on the board but price at $0.31 and $1.57 per million blended (board cost over board tokens), which puts even the reduced set above the ceiling; Claude Code pinned by CLI version is the alternative harness (the board prices GLM-5.3-Flash under it at $0.36 per trial) and is recorded as the fallback if mini-SWE-agent's token use makes model A alone exceed $0.8k. Sandbox hours: 954 trials times the board's mini-SWE-agent mean trial duration (1,689-1,995 s) is about 450-530 sandbox-hours, priced at step 0 from the provider's page; GPU tasks exist ('Terminal-Bench includes GPU and multi-container tasks', Hub README) and their count is read from the task configs at step 0, with 20 GPU-hours as the ceiling. Trials per task are not the lever: the task-cluster interval is bounded by between-task heterogeneity on 19 tasks ($k = 5$ narrows $\delta$'s half-width from 0.139 to 0.120 at two models); a third model is the lever (kill power 0.62 to 0.78 at +50% cost).
killing_experiment.kills_if: First clause, pre-registered on $\delta^{\ast}$ (E3; the DiD $\delta$ of E4 reported beside it): DEAD if the 95% task-cluster bootstrap interval of $\delta^{\ast}$, pooled over the two models, lies entirely below 0.15 pass-rate points and $\delta$'s upper end is also below 0.15 — the fixed tasks moved by less than one trial in seven beyond the recalibration lift, inside the identical-rerun flip band (2610.11678: 15-36% of outcomes) and below the half line for any recalibration lift at or above 0.043 (E5); the Terminal-Bench team's reading ('fewer agent timeouts and errors than 3.0, reducing measurement noise') stands with a number. ESTABLISHED if $\delta^{\ast}$'s lower end is above 0 and $\hat\pi > 0.5$ at the point estimate with $\Delta_{\mathrm{kept}}$'s interval excluding zero; the 0.5 share line with its own lower end above 0.5 is declared only when met. NOT RESOLVED otherwise: a pre-registered outcome, reported with every interval and the per-model estimates. Power check (power_check field; 19 repaired, 47 untouched, 3 trials, 2 models, stratified task bootstrap): the half-width of $\delta^{\ast}$ is 0.10-0.15 points; the kill fires in 62% of simulated null datasets (true $\delta^{\ast} = 0.02$) and 1% of expected datasets (true 0.23); 'established' fires in 93% of expected and 7% of null datasets; the share's interval straddles 0.5 in 77-91% of datasets in every scenario except strong repair (true share 0.90: straddles 31%), so the claim's written 0.5 line is resolvable at this design only when the repaired tasks move by about 0.3 points with recalibration near zero — the claims stage is asked to carry the headline as $\delta^{\ast} > 0.15$ with the share beside it (claim_attachment_note). Second clause (step 1): DEAD if $\rho_{RU} \ge c_{0.05}$ under the difficulty-matched null (the repaired tasks order the board as any difficulty-matched 19-task subset does); PARKED, not dead, if step 0 finds no per-task vector on the job pages (trigger in data_gate). The claim is a conjunction, so either clause's death kills it; the kill report's 'AND' form is replaced because a blocked step 1 would have made the claim unkillable. Both outcomes of the first clause are informative: the kill is the first measured version-pair decomposition of an agent benchmark (zero in print) and the owner's noise-reduction sentence with an interval; the established result is the repair channel's first number and the launch-table deltas across 3.0 to 4.0 re-read as repair.

power_check.run: 2026-11-02, scratchpad/power/power_check.py and power2.py (simulation, not evidence about the world): per-task 4.0 pass probabilities for a mid-board model drawn as 40% all-fail, 12% saturated, rest uniform on [0.05, 0.95] (repaired set: 20% all-fail); 3.0 pass = 4.0 pass minus a recalibration shift on intermediate tasks (untouched) and times (1 - r_t) with r_t Beta-distributed (repaired); k Bernoulli trials per cell; stratified task bootstrap, B = 1000; 150 datasets per scenario.

half_widths_k3_M2.share_median: 0.49-0.53 (mean larger: the denominator crosses zero in draws)

scenarios_k3_M2.name: S3 null (no repair effect, recalibration 0.05 on both)

power_check.levers: M = 1: delta half-width 0.14-0.17, kill power at null 0.36. M = 3: half-width 0.09-0.14, kill power 0.78, established 0.96 under S1. k = 5 at M = 2: half-width 0.120 (heterogeneity-bound). The second model is the lever; trials per task are not.
power_check.reading: The 0.5 share line is not resolvable with 19 repaired tasks except under strong repair; the repair effect in pass-rate points is. The scenario S4 (recalibration lifts both sets, repaired a little more) is the one the design distinguishes worst from S1 (kill fires 6%, established 58%): there the hybrid arm's gamma_R against mean delta_U is the discriminating readout, not delta alone.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment p 0.45: $\delta^{\ast}$ between 0.15 and 0.30 (fixes convert tasks that failed for flakiness or misspecification in 3.0 into tasks a mid-board model passes one to two trials in three), $\bar\Delta_U$ between 0 and 0.05 (the 8-hour flat timeout and the calibrated CPU and memory remove a few timeout- and OOM-ended trials; the release note: frontier models 'never or rarely encounter timeouts now'), $\gamma_R$ within 0.05 of $\bar\Delta_U$, $\hat\pi$ above 0.5 at the point estimate with the interval straddling 0.5, and the composition term positive (the two saturated tasks removed were passes). Ordering clause, judgment p 0.4: $\rho_{RU}$ below the matched ceiling, because the repaired tasks reward the behaviours the flaky versions punished.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Terminal-Bench team, 4.0 release note (fetched 2026-11-02): 'TB 4.0 has fewer agent timeouts and errors than 3.0, reducing measurement noise.' and 'By running the tasks with a large amount of resource headroom, we can select a reasonable setting that does not impact the final metrics.' — the recalibration is the change and is metric-neutral, the fixes are hygiene. ABA 2605.26079 (kill report, full text): 'Terminal-Bench 2 reshuffles more aggressively than swe_bench_verified: a non-trivial share of the public task set is flagged, lifting per-model scores by several percentage points and moving multiple submissions by three or more rank positions' — broken tasks are the lift and the reshuffle, measured by filtering. Anthropic, 'Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals' (2026-02-05, fetched 2026-11-02): 'the gap between the most- and least-resourced setups on Terminal-Bench 2.0 was 6 percentage points (p < 0.01)', 'From 1x through 3x, success scores fluctuate within the margins of noise (p=0.40)', 'The same trends seem to hold on models other than Claude, but we haven't rigorously tested them' — resource headroom alone moves a model by up to 6 points, so the recalibration channel is not assumed small by everyone. 2609.02899 (abstract): contamination 'inflates scores but rarely reorders' (rank correlation 0.997) — the prior that a uniform lift leaves orderings alone.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: (a) $\delta^{\ast} \geq 0.15$ with $\hat\pi > 0.5$: a launch-table delta across 3.0 to 4.0 is a reread of the 19 fixed tasks, and every continuous benchmark owes a repair delta per release; ABA's filtering lift is reproduced by a repair. (b) The kill: the untouched tasks carry the delta and the fixes moved nothing beyond rerun noise — the owners' sentence with an interval, and the Anthropic resource channel, not the audit channel, is what a refresh moves; aggregators keep the trend line with a recalibration footnote. (c) $\gamma_R$ far from $\bar\Delta_U$ (parallel trends fail by more than 0.05): the recalibration is not uniform across tasks, so the DiD any lab would compute from its own both-version logs is biased by $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$; this is a result about the method labs would use and is citable on its own. (d) Ordering: $\rho_{RU}$ below the matched ceiling while $\delta^{\ast}$ is small — the fixes reorder without lifting, the case neither ABA nor 2609.02899 describes.

identifiability: Random given: the two task packages (Hub revisions 1 and 4, immutable; the hybrid arm's resource edit is a recorded file diff), the harness at one commit with its prompts and tools, the model checkpoint id and provider endpoint, the temperature set explicitly in the harness config (above zero and reported; temperature 0 through an API is not a deterministic arm), the sandbox provider and concurrency, and the calendar window of the run. Whose temperature: only the model samples; Terminal-Bench verifiers are scripts run on the end state (deterministic given the end state; no LLM judge, no simulated user), so a verifier outcome is a decision plus the channels named next, never luck. Sources of randomness after the action, each named and logged: (i) the model's sampling at the stated temperature plus provider nondeterminism; (ii) the wall-clock channel — trials ending by agent timeout, out-of-memory or resource kill depend on host load and API latency (Anthropic 2026-02-05: 'pass rates fluctuate with time of day'), which is why end reasons are logged per trial, $\bar\Delta_U$ is reported with and without wall-clock-ended trials, and the six cells of a task run in one window with arms alternating; (iii) image drift for environments that fetch packages at build or run time (2610.14460: rebuilt images changed 0.83% of three-run majority verdicts), pinned by image digest where the package allows and otherwise logged; (iv) GPU tasks' kernel nondeterminism. Whose property: $\delta^{\ast}$, $\gamma_R$ and $\bar\Delta_U$ are properties of (version pair, model, harness commit, temperature, sandbox provider, window); $\hat\pi$ is a property of the version pair for that system; the step-1 ordering is a property of the 4.0 board as shipped (each vendor's own harness, unstated temperature, 5 trials; the board's own accuracy_ci95_half_width column is 2.45-3.94 points), so it says how the board orders entries, not how models order. The parallel-trends assumption behind the DiD ($\gamma_R = \bar\Delta_U$) is measured by the hybrid arm, not assumed; the repaired tasks were selected for flakiness, and flakiness correlates with resource caps, so $\gamma_R > \bar\Delta_U$ is the expected direction of the bias in any DiD-only design. Conditioning set for the ordering null: the null is drawn from the same matrix with the same ties and the same five-trial cells, so it carries the board's run noise by construction and no parametric noise model is assumed.

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: the Terminal-Bench 4.0 release note lists 19 fixed and 8 removed tasks and a flat 8-hour timeout, says 'These represent breaking changes that require re-running trials', and gives no number comparing 3.0 and 4.0 for any model; the Terminal-Bench position post: 'Reuse, regrade, and rerun trials as necessary, in that order' (the per-task diff as infrastructure, no number); Anthropic's infrastructure-noise post measured the resource channel on 2.0 (+6 points, infra errors 5.8% to 0.5%) and recommends evals 'specify both parameters per task'; ABA reads the maintainers' fix PR as ground truth for 'repaired' and stops at fixed commits (App. G). Who pays: the Terminal-Bench team (the 5.0 diff protocol and the 4.1 verifier fixes), labs whose launch tables cite 3.0 and 4.0 numbers side by side, evaluators (Vals, Artificial Analysis) plotting across the refresh, the ABA line (an audit's lift versus a repair's lift).

impact_ceiling.floor: The first measured version-pair decomposition of an agent benchmark — $\delta^{\ast}$, $\gamma_R$, $\bar\Delta_U$, $\hat\pi$, the composition term and the verifier-only re-grade for two models — cited at the next refresh and by the audit line either way. Requires step 0 to pass and step 2 to run. p 0.55 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The repair channel established ($\delta^{\ast}$'s lower end above 0, $\hat\pi > 0.5$) and the ordering clause beyond the matched ceiling on the 35-entry board; the Terminal-Bench team ships a repair delta and the untouched-subset ordering with 5.0 and one owner community changes its release note. Requires step 1's data and the team's adoption. p 0.25 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Repair delta per release becomes the reporting rule for continuous benchmarks (Terminal-Bench, SWE-Bench Pro, tau-bench) and launch tables carry two columns per refresh. Requires the middle result replicated on a second pair (4.0 to 4.1's verifier fixes, or 5.0) and one lab adopting the columns. p 0.1 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L1 direct (benchmark validity and churn). HAL / Narayanan route: direct (evaluators; paused trackers; the ABA line sits in the same lane). Narasimhan route: tau-bench 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 is the next version pair for the same 2x2 design. Industry: labs' evaluation teams reading refreshes; benchmark owners. Jacob's edge: the design-of-experiments content (a 2x2 on the repaired tasks, an exact decomposition, a stratified null, the power arithmetic) is hand-checkable; no numerics, no training. zero_where: L2, L3, L4, L5; the systems route; frontier post-training teams (a measurement of their published numbers, not their recipe).
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 0 ($0, 2 d), then step 2 (at most $1.5k, 0-20 GPU-h, 10 d): dead if the 95% task-cluster bootstrap interval of $\delta^{\ast}$ lies below 0.15 pass-rate points (kill power 0.62 under the null, false-kill rate 0.01 under the expected scenario); step 1 ($0, 2 d, behind the job-page gate): the ordering clause dead if $\rho_{RU} \geq c_{0.05}$ of the difficulty-matched null. Time to the first-clause verdict: 14 days.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Concept-level kill search 2026-11-01 (data/reports/2026-W44-kill-CL-W44-02.md): 16 arXiv API queries with mechanism and role words, 18 in-window neighbours opened, 0 on the shipped-version-pair unit; adjacent audit, filter and re-grade lane about 0.35 papers per week. Closest, in their own words: ABA 2605.26079 App. G, 'Findings also reflect a snapshot at fixed commits ... any downstream ranking shifts should be read as ABA's estimates relative to the versions audited rather than as ground truth'; 2601.08778 section 5.5, rankings 'have a weak correlation with the rankings on the corrected Dev subset (r_s=0.32, p=0.23)' and 'We advocate that future work use SAR-Agent and SAPAR to develop high-quality text-to-SQL benchmarks'; 2609.00482 abstract, 'Equally short matched-random subtests provide a baseline for variation due to item subsampling' on five static benchmarks; the recalibration channel measured once, by Anthropic on 2.0 for its own models ('The same trends seem to hold on models other than Claude, but we haven't rigorously tested them'). Incumbents: the Terminal-Bench team (owns the 3.0 per-trial record, the Hub and the 5.0 diff protocol; its release note shows no cross-version number), ABA's authors (own the audit tool; filter-level only), Anthropic's eval infrastructure team (resource channel on 2.0, one model family). Pre-window precedents with tricks: Northcutt 2103.14749 (correct test labels; ResNet-18 beats ResNet-50 at +6% mislabel prevalence), SWE-bench+ 2410.06992 (32.67% leakage, 31.08% weak tests; 12.47% to 3.97%), MMLU-Redux 2406.04127 (6.49% error estimate), OpenAI SWE-bench Verified 2024-08 (68.3% filtered; GPT-4o 16% to 33.2%), UTBoost 2506.09289 (345 erroneous passes; 11 ranking changes), AndroidControl-Curated 2510.18488 (+15 points on the purified version) — every one a filter or re-grade whose same-model delta is the headline, never split against an untouched set under a re-run. Race: the owner's release cycle (3.0 to 4.0 about two months; 4.1 and 5.0 milestones live) against 3 weeks to the first-clause verdict.
scorecard.why_now: Terminal-Bench 4.0 (registry created 2026-08-27; board payload last updated 2026-10-23) with both revisions addressable on the Harbor Hub and a per-task changelog; the recalibration methodology published 2026-02-05 (Anthropic); the matched-random null 2026-08-31 (2609.00482); the rerun flip band 2026-10-08 (2610.11678). The decomposition itself is a 2x2 and a paired difference, decades old; the enabling piece is the addressable version pair, and the flag that nothing else is new is recorded.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement (a version-pair decomposition on a 2x2 arm and a composition-matched ordering test) with a reporting-rule consequence. It is not a benchmark, not an audit tool, not a contamination study, not a harness comparison, not an equating study (import S5xF2 tests the old-to-new link's population invariance; this probe tests the repair channel on one pair), and not a claim about any model's ability.

verdict_by_position.solo: proposed; the claim survived its concept-level kill search 2026-11-01 (weak); this probe's design red team is owed before any dollar is spent; about $1.5k and 14 days from public packages, inside Gate 1; the race is the owner inside one release cycle.

objections.persona: theory; checklist:2026-10-20 (a red team of a zero-cost probe runs its first step)
objections.objection: The ordering clause is dead on the shipped 4.0 board under the record's own pre-registration. Step 1 was run exactly as E9 writes it (35 entries x 66 tasks x 5 trials, strata by quartile of board-wide 4.0 pass rate, B = 4000): $\rho_{RU} = 0.902$ against a difficulty-matched ceiling $c_{0.05} = 0.839$ (null median 0.913); $\rho_{RU}$ sits at the 37th percentile of the null, and the one-row-per-model secondary gives 0.930 against 0.882 (48th percentile). The repaired tasks order the board as any difficulty-matched 19-task subset does. The record says 'DEAD if $\rho_{RU} \ge c_{0.05}$' and 'the claim is a conjunction, so either clause's death kills it'; the claim as written (CL-W44-02 headline, second clause) is therefore dead, and the pre-registered surprise (d) 'the fixes reorder without lifting' is excluded.
objections.evidence: hub.harborframework.com server action fetchLeaderboardRowTrials on all 35 rows of leaderboard 4-0-0 (11,550 trials, saved dl/trials/, assembled dl/all_trials.json); sim/real_did.py, sim/real_did_out.txt; the record's E9 and kills_if
objections.answer: conceded: the pre-registered test fired on real data. I re-ran sim/real_did.py with python3 -I on the downloaded 4.0 payload (35 entries x 66 tasks x 5 trials) and reproduced it exactly as E9 writes it: $\rho_{RU} = 0.902$ against the difficulty-matched ceiling $c_{0.05} = 0.839$ (null median 0.913, $\rho_{RU}$ at the 37th percentile); one row per (agent, model), 23 rows: 0.930 against 0.882 (48th percentile); the unstratified ceiling 0.832 is also cleared. Step 1 was conditional only on data-gate item (4), which passed, and the record wrote 'DEAD if $\rho_{RU} \ge c_{0.05}$'. No pre-registered variant remains to report; a different statistic or stratification now would be fishing. The record's own identifiability field said the ordering clause is a property of the 4.0 board as shipped, and on that board the 19 repaired tasks order entries as any difficulty-matched 19-task subset does. The second clause of CL-W44-02 is dead on this pair, and because the claim's headline is a conjunction the claim as written is dead; the first clause goes to the claims layer as a new candidate (defender.md).

objections.persona: theory; systems; checklist:2026-11-01 (free paired trials checked against the host's registry)
objections.objection: The first clause's pre-registered kill fires on free data the record says does not exist. Harbor Hub revision 1 registers a 'Terminal-Bench 3.0' leaderboard (3-0-0) with 12 rows of 370 per-trial, per-task records (74 tasks x 5; reward, error_type, timestamps, tokens, agent_version), and seven (agent, model, effort) entries sit on both boards. Pooled over them with the task-cluster bootstrap of E8: $\bar\Delta_R = +0.088$ [+0.014, +0.162], $\bar\Delta_U = +0.016$ [-0.006, +0.037], DiD $\delta = +0.072$ [-0.005, +0.149]; the DiD clause of the kill (upper end below 0.15) fires, 'established' (lower end above 0) fails, and the share is 0.57 [-0.07, +1.31]. The two caveats (vendor harnesses with version drift; the 3.0 trials are the record the owners selected the fixes on, so $\bar\Delta_R$ carries regression to the mean upward) both bias this number against the kill, not toward it. Excluding None-reward trials moves the upper end to 0.155 and the lower end to +0.0005: a knife edge, which is the 'not resolved' outcome, not 'established'.
objections.evidence: fetchLeaderboardWithRows on revision 1 (dl/action_lb3.json: 12 rows) and revision 4 (dl/action_lb4.json: 35 rows); fetchLeaderboardRowTrials on all 47 rows (15,990 trials); sim/real_did_out.txt; record fields data_gate (4), why_now, red_team_preanswers ('the 3.0 board is gone'), kill report section 5 ('the 3.0 per-trial results are not public')
objections.answer: Two concessions first. (i) The record's 'the 3.0 board is gone; the preserved asset is the package' and the kill report's section 5 ('the 3.0 per-trial results are not public') are false: dl/rsc_rev1.txt carries leaderboard '3-0-0', 'Terminal-Bench 3.0', 12 rows of 370 trials, and the seven matched entries are real. (ii) The record's 'expected' magnitude ($\delta^{\ast}$ between 0.15 and 0.30) is too large: the free record puts the repair effect at 0.07 to 0.13 points depending on the cut, so the 0.15 kill line sits on the point estimate, which is a calibration defect of the probe. What the evidence does not compel is the sentence 'the first clause's pre-registered kill fires'. (a) The pre-registered kill is a conjunction: the $\delta^{\ast}$ interval (hybrid arm) below 0.15 AND the DiD upper end below 0.15. The free record has no hybrid arm, so $\delta^{\ast}$ is not estimable from it and the pre-registered kill cannot fire on it; what fired is the DiD half, under one of two counting rules (None = 0: upper end 0.149; None excluded: 0.155), which the objection itself calls a knife edge. Under the record's three-outcome rule that is NOT RESOLVED, not DEAD. (b) The pooled-over-7 number includes two entries outside the regime the record pre-registered on 2026-11-01, before the payload was pulled ('two models in the 25-45% band'; 'saturated and all-fail strata reported separately because they cannot move'): Sonnet 5 (13.6% on 3.0, 12.4% on 4.0) and GPT-5.6 Luna (13.3%, 17.3%), for which 10 and 12 of the 19 repaired tasks are all-fail in both versions (defsim/checks.py, run on dl/all_trials.json). Their $\bar\Delta_R$ is +0.014 against $\bar\Delta_U$ +0.034: a floor, not a repair effect. On the five entries at or above 20% on both boards the pooled DiD is +0.109 [+0.008, +0.211] with share 0.79; on the strict 25-45% band (three entries) +0.117 [-0.013, +0.248], share 0.86; on the file-diff's substantive 14-task repaired set, five entries, +0.133 [+0.012, +0.253], share 0.71. In the pre-registered regime the DiD kill does not fire, 'established' (lower end above 0) fires at one band edge and not at the other, and the share's point estimate is 0.7 to 0.9. The 20% cut is mine (the record's band is 25-45% on 4.0 accuracy, which leaves two matched entries); the objective reason for the cut is the all-fail count, 10-12 of 19 for the excluded entries against 4 of 19 for Fable 5, Sol and Terra. (c) The claim's own first-clause quantifier is the share $\hat\pi > 0.5$, equivalently $\delta^{\ast} > 3.47\,\bar\Delta_U$ under parallel trends (E5); at the observed $\bar\Delta_U$ of 0.01 to 0.016 the half line sits at $\delta^{\ast} \approx 0.03$ to $0.055$, which every cut's point estimate clears; the 0.15 line coincides with the half line only at $\bar\Delta_U = 0.043$. So on the free record the first clause is alive and unresolved, its effect size is 0.07 to 0.13 points, and the two caveats the objection names (vendor-harness version change on every matched entry; selection of the 19 on these same 3.0 trials, regression to the mean upward) are the reason the pinned-harness re-run with a fresh (3,3) arm is still the instrument.

objections.persona: theory
objections.objection: The quantity the probe pre-registers is not a property of the version pair: on the free record the DiD flips sign between entries, from $-0.072$ [-0.140, -0.009] for Codex/GPT-5.6 Luna (repaired tasks moved 0.000 while untouched tasks rose 0.072) to $+0.218$ [+0.021, +0.408] for Claude Code/Fable 5, with Grok 4.6 at $-0.025$ and Sonnet 5 at $+0.032$. A two-model probe whose pooled $\delta^{\ast}$ interval decides life or death is then decided by which two open-weight models are chosen, and 'with the model fixed' in the headline hides a model-by-version interaction larger than the effect. The claim needs a quantifier over models (for every entry, or for the mean over a named population) before its kill is meaningful.
objections.evidence: sim/real_did_out.txt per-entry rows; record identifiability field ('$\delta^{\ast}$ ... properties of (version pair, model, harness ...)') against the headline 'the 19 repaired tasks carry more than half of the kept-task delta'
objections.answer: The sign flips are at the floor of the pass-rate band, not a model-by-version interaction in the band the record pre-registered. GPT-5.6 Luna's $\bar\Delta_R$ is exactly 0.000 because 12 of the 19 repaired tasks are all-fail for it in both versions (Sonnet 5: 10 of 19); a task that is unsolvable before and after a repair cannot carry a repair effect, which the record's regime field wrote down as 'saturated and all-fail strata reported separately because they cannot move'. Grok 4.6's $-0.025$ [$-0.176$, $+0.116$] is inside noise under a harness regression of 6 points on every set (agent 1.0.0 to 1.0.5; its all-fail count on R is 10 of 19 as well). Among the entries above 20% on both boards the DiD is positive for four of five (+0.218, +0.158, +0.098, +0.095) and the pooled interval excludes zero (+0.109 [+0.008, +0.211]); the non-overlapping per-entry intervals the objection cites (Luna's upper end $-0.009$ against Fable 5's lower end $+0.021$) are the floor entry against an in-band entry. Conceded within this answer: 'with the model fixed' is not a quantifier, and the headline has to carry the band it is quantified over. That is the record's regime field made explicit, a scope restriction that leaves the mechanism and the quantity unchanged: the surviving sentence reads 'for a model in the band where the repaired tasks are passable (20-45% accuracy under the pinned harness, 4.0 all-fail share on R below one half)', and objection 19's pilot is how the band is checked before a dollar is spent. The probe already reports per-model estimates with the model as a fixed factor; the band makes the pooled estimate a statement about a named population, which is what the objection asks for.

objections.persona: theory; checklist: estimator unbiased for the stated objective
objections.objection: $\delta^{\ast} = p(4,4) - p(3,4)$ does not estimate the repair effect, because the 4.0.0 package differs from 3.0.0 on every kept task in more than timeout, CPU and memory: (i) every instruction.md's budget sentence changed ('You have 7200 seconds to complete this task' became 'You have 28800 seconds' on all 66; 3.0 values 1800-28800 s), a prompt change the model reads; (ii) 4.0.0 task.toml pins the environment image by digest ('docker_image = ...@sha256:...') and 4.0.0 compose files replace 'build:' with pinned sidecar images, while 3.0.0 builds from Dockerfiles at run time (image drift, 2610.14460's 0.83%); (iii) 4.0.0 adds a '[verifier.environment]' block (separate verifier container with its own CPU/memory/image) that 3.0.0 lacks on 60 of 66 tasks. The hybrid arm as specified swaps only the task.toml resource fields, so $\delta^{\ast} = $ repair $+$ (pinned vs built images) $+$ (verifier separation) $+$ (stated budget, unless the instruction is also edited, which makes the hybrid a content edit). The named quantity is estimable only if the hybrid is built as 4.0.0 with the content diff reverted (reverse-patch), not 3.0.0 with resources edited; as written the estimator does not estimate $\delta^{\ast}$.
objections.evidence: dl/tasks/*.task.toml (140 files; e.g. cad-model 3 vs 4 diff: agent timeout 7200 -> 28800, cpus 1 -> 2, memory 2048 -> 8192, added [verifier.environment] and docker_image digests); dl/instr/* (66 pairs; budget sentence on all); dl/envf/*compose.yaml (build: -> image:@sha256 on payments-pipeline-fix, live-database-cutover, nextjs-performance); record E1/E3 and data_gate (2)
objections.answer: Conceded on the arm as written: 'swap only the task.toml resource fields' does not produce $\delta^{\ast}$, because the diff shows the recalibration is a bundle applied to all 66 kept tasks: the budget sentence in every instruction.md, a pinned image digest on every environment, and a [verifier.environment] block on 60 of 66 (verified on dl/tasks/uefi-bootkit.{3,4}.task.toml: the 4.0 file adds the verifier block with memory 16384 and the digest, and changes timeout 7200 to 28800 and memory 8192 to 16384, nothing else). The fix is to the probe, not the claim. Define $r$ in E1 as the uniform-change bundle, and build the hybrid arm $(3,4)$ as the 3.0.0 task content plus every change that 4.0.0 applied to all tasks alike: the task.toml resource fields, the budget sentence (the same one-line edit 4.0 made), the task's own 4.0.0 [verifier.environment] block, and the pinned 4.0.0 image wherever the environment files are unchanged. Then $(3,4) - (3,3) = \gamma_R$ is the bundle on the repaired tasks and $(4,4) - (3,4) = \delta^{\ast}$ is the task-specific repair. The residue: on the repaired tasks whose environment files changed (7 of the 14 substantive ones: intrastat-meldung, legacy-utility-triage, math-eval-grader, vf2-speedup-networkx, medical-claims-processing, kv-live-surgery, heat-pump-warranty, with batched-eval-parity and vba-userform-port touching environment too) the 4.0 digest image contains the repair, so the hybrid builds from the 3.0.0 Dockerfile and $\delta^{\ast}$ on those tasks carries pinned-versus-rebuilt alongside the repair; that residue is bounded by 2610.14460's figure for rebuilt images, 0.83% of three-run majority verdicts, eighteen times below the 0.15 line. The objection's own alternative (4.0.0 reverse-patched) is the same arm for instruction and verifier repairs and is not constructible for environment repairs baked into the digest image, so the two constructions differ only on that residue. With the bundle definition the estimator estimates the named quantity, the parallel-trends check $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$ keeps its meaning, and data-gate item (2) is rewritten to confirm the four edits, not one.

objections.persona: professor; checklist: premise numbers verbatim; checklist:2026-10-20 (open the release's data layout)
objections.objection: The labelled sets are not what the data gate assumes ('exactly the tasks named by the task README changelogs differ in instruction, environment or verifier files while the others differ only in resource settings'). The 4.0 README change logs reproduce 19/47/8, but they are PR history: uefi-bootkit (R, '#1530 Increased verifier boot and total timeouts') has no content diff between 3.0.0 and 4.0.0 (identical file list and sizes, identical instruction after the budget sentence, identical verifier timeouts); four more R tasks are cosmetic (interleaved-vigenere #1739 and glycan-ms2-elucidation #1741 change Markdown headings only; vpp-loss-divergence #1529 adds a Dockerfile syntax line; layout-config-recreation2 #1781/#1784 pins a Google-Fonts revision). Seven U tasks have file changes: three compose image pins, distributed-dedup (5 .crc files removed), embedding-drift-monitor, shadow-relay, and cumulative-layout-shift, which removes environment/barber-shop-site/.claude/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md and adds three UI components, a skill file a Claude-Code-family harness loads (that task is a top-4 U mover on the free record, +0.143). With 5 of 19 R tasks unable to move by repair, a true per-substantive-task effect of 0.20 gives $\delta^{\ast} \approx 0.15$, on the kill line, so the 'expected' scenario (0.23 across all 19) is implausible by construction; the sets must be the file diff's (R about 14, with uefi-bootkit moved to U), and the probe's power recomputed on them.
objections.evidence: dl/task_crawl.json (change logs and file lists for all 140 task-revisions), dl/sets.json, dl/instr_summary.json; release note 'We fixed 19 tasks'
objections.answer: Accepted, and adopted as the labelling. Verified: uefi-bootkit's instruction is identical after the budget sentence is normalised and its task.toml differs only in resources and the uniform 4.0 additions (my diff above), so its '#1530' change-log line is PR history; dl/instr_summary.json marks 8 of 19 R instructions identical after normalisation, and the four cosmetic tasks are as the objection says. The primary sets are the file diff's: $R$ = 14 tasks with a substantive instruction, environment or verifier change; uefi-bootkit moves to $U$ ($n_U = 48$); the four cosmetic tasks form a declared label-only stratum reported beside both sets and pooled into neither; the change-log 19/47 labelling is reported as the secondary so the owner's count stays visible. On the free record this relabelling moves the mid-band DiD from +0.109 to +0.133 [+0.012, +0.253] and widens the interval as $\sqrt{19/14}$ predicts. Conceded with it: the expected scenario of 0.23 across all 19 was implausible by construction; the power field is recomputed on $n_R = 14$ (objection 6 and defender.md). The cumulative-layout-shift finding (a Claude-Code skill file removed from an 'untouched' task that moved +0.143) is recorded as a U-side content change and that task is flagged in the per-task table; it is one task of 48 and does not change the set definition.

objections.persona: theory; checklist:2026-10-20 (compute what the design scores under the record's own noise model before pre-registering)
objections.objection: The power numbers in the record were not computed on the kill as written. power_check.py and power2.py never simulate the (3,4) hybrid cell; they compute the DiD $\delta$ only and the record reports its kill rate as '$\delta^{\ast}$' ('the kill fires in 62% of simulated null datasets (true $\delta^{\ast}$ = 0.02)' — the 0.02 is the DiD under a null where $\delta^{\ast}$ = 0 and $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$ = 0.02). Re-simulated with the hybrid arm and the conjunction (interval of $\delta^{\ast}$ below 0.15 AND $\delta$'s upper end below 0.15), k = 3, M = 2: null 0.62 / expected 0.01 hold for the conjunction by coincidence, because the binding clause of the AND is the DiD's wider interval (the $\delta^{\ast}$ clause alone kills 92% of null datasets). 'Pre-registered on $\delta^{\ast}$ with $\delta$ beside it' is inverted in effect, and the 'true $\delta^{\ast}$ = 0.23' of S1 is 0.20. Under the magnitudes the free record shows (repair about 0.07, recalibration about 0.016) the design returns P[kill] = 0.19, P[established] = 0.13, P[not resolved] = 0.68 at M = 2 (0.40 / 0.12 / 0.48 at M = 3): in the most likely world the $1.5k probe resolves nothing, which fails Gate 1's 'both outcomes informative'.
objections.evidence: scratchpad/power/power_check.py and power2.py (no (3,4) cell; stats() returns mean_U, mean_R, delta, kept, share); sim/power_recheck.py and sim/power_recheck_out.txt; record power_check field
objections.answer: conceded: I read scratchpad/power/power_check.py; its stats() returns (mean_U, mean_R, delta, kept, share) from DU and DR only, there is no (3,4) cell, and the record reported the DiD's kill rate as '$\delta^{\ast}$'. The attackers' sim/power_recheck.py with the hybrid arm shows the conjunction's 0.62 / 0.01 are the DiD clause's numbers (the $\delta^{\ast}$ clause alone kills 92% of null datasets), so 'pre-registered on $\delta^{\ast}$ with $\delta$ beside it' was inverted in effect, and S1's 'true $\delta^{\ast}$ = 0.23' is 0.20. Corrections adopted for the surviving probe: the kill is on $\delta^{\ast}$ alone, the DiD is reported beside it, and the power field is replaced by the re-check's numbers. I re-ran the attackers' script on the file-diff sets ($n_R = 14$, $n_U = 48$, defsim/power_r14.py): a true null (no repair, recalibration 0.016) is killed in 86% of datasets at $M = 2$ and 98% at $M = 3$; at the magnitude the mid-band free record shows (true $\delta^{\ast}$ about 0.08-0.09 under the empirical difficulty model) the $\delta^{\ast}$ kill fires in 23-39% and 'established' in 10-26%, so the probe resolves the first clause in under half of the datasets of the most likely world. That is the objection's point and it stands: at $1.5k the probe is a measurement with intervals (the first pinned-harness decomposition, cited either way) and a reliable kill of a true null, not a reliable verdict on a 0.1-point repair effect; $M = 3$ is the lever and $k$ is not.

objections.persona: professor; checklist: 'why now' names the enabling piece; 'no reason' is a flag
objections.objection: The 'why not done' argument ('the 3.0 per-trial results are not public, so the first clause needs a paid re-run, which the zero-cost audit lane has not funded') collapses: the Hub serves both boards' per-trial records and ships a row-comparison action ('Compare (n)' on selected rows; fetchLeaderboardRowComparison), so the Terminal-Bench team and any reader can compute $\delta$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{kept}}$, the composition term and the cross-version ordering on seven matched entries in an afternoon. The remaining reason nobody has published the number is 'no reason', the checklist's red flag; and the solo position's race is against anyone with a browser, not against one owner inside a release cycle. The paid re-run buys only the pinned harness and the hybrid arm, and the hybrid arm is the part objection 4 says is mis-specified.
objections.evidence: dl/js/*.js (server action ids and the LeaderboardCompareButton component), dl/action_lb3.json, dl/action_lb4.json; kill report section 5; record why_now and verdict_by_position
objections.answer: Conceded on the fact: the 3.0 per-trial record is served by the Hub, the kill report's section 5 sentence is false, the row-comparison action exists, and the 7-entry DiD is an afternoon's work for anyone — I did it in one (defsim/checks.py), and it goes into the record. Not conceded: that the remaining reason is 'no reason'. The free-record number is a confounded knife edge by three named channels — every matched entry changed agent version between boards (Claude Code 2.1.207 to 2.1.231, Codex 0.144.1 to 0.149.1, Grok Build 1.0.0 to 1.0.5), the 19 fixes were selected on these same 3.0 trials (regression to the mean on $\bar\Delta_R$), and 5 trials per cell — and it has no hybrid arm, so it cannot separate $\delta^{\ast}$ from $\gamma_R$. A number that flips between counting rules and between band cuts is not a publishable decomposition, and that is a reason nobody has published it. The enabling piece for the re-run is unchanged (revision 1 addressable as 3.0.0 on the Hub; a per-task changelog). What the objection does change is the solo position's race: the free-record DiD is now public knowledge for anyone with a browser, so the solo value sits entirely in the pinned-harness paired re-run with the hybrid arm, and the record's why_now and race lines are rewritten to say so.

objections.persona: professor; checklist: mechanism and consequence written before the run
objections.objection: The mechanism sentence ('fixes convert tasks that failed for flakiness or misspecification in 3.0 into tasks a mid-board model passes one to two trials in three') is contradicted on the free record: 4 of 19 repaired tasks moved down for the matched entries (vf2-speedup-networkx $-0.286$ — '#1582 Updated oracle, native-build portability, and verifier speed gate'; kv-live-surgery $-0.101$ — '#1649 Enforced response correctness and binary rewards in the verifier'; ctr-optimization $-0.057$ — '#1585 Fixed verifier coverage'; layout-config-recreation2 $-0.057$), 3 moved zero, and one task (intrastat-meldung, +0.486) carries a quarter of $\bar\Delta_R$. A repair that tightens a verifier lowers the pass rate; the signed mean $\delta^{\ast}$ cancels lifts against tightenings and a 'repair share' of a signed sum is not the quantity the consequence ('a launch-table delta is a reread of the 19 fixed tasks') needs. Pre-register the sign per task from the change-log channel (verifier tightening vs instruction clarification) or report $\sum_t |\Delta_t|$ by channel.
objections.evidence: sim/real_did_out.txt per-task rows; dl/task_crawl.json change-log text; record preregistered_surprise.expected
objections.answer: The signed mean is the right primary quantity for the claim's consequence, and the addition the objection asks for is adopted. A launch table reports a signed delta; the claim says that delta is a reread of the fixed tasks; a verifier tightening that lowers a task's pass rate (kv-live-surgery, '#1649 enforced response correctness and binary rewards') is a repair effect with the opposite sign and belongs in the signed sum, because the launch-table delta it explains is also signed. Conceded inside this: the mechanism sentence in preregistered_surprise ('fixes convert tasks that failed for flakiness or misspecification into tasks a mid-board model passes one to two trials in three') is contradicted on the free record — 4 of 19 repaired tasks moved down, 3 moved zero, and intrastat-meldung (+0.486) carries a quarter of $\bar\Delta_R$. The surviving probe pre-registers a sign per repaired task from the change-log channel (verifier tightening: negative or zero; instruction clarification or environment fix: positive), reports $\sum_{t \in R} |\Delta_t|$ by channel beside the signed mean, and reports $\delta^{\ast}$ with intrastat-meldung held out so one task's weight is visible.

objections.persona: theory; checklist: Gate 0 (every defined quantity's conditioning set; verifier outcome type)
objections.objection: E1 assumes $y \in \{0, 1\}$ and the data gate assumes a verifier script returns a pass; the Hub record has fractional rewards on kv-live-surgery (6 trials in 3.0; a repaired task whose repair is 'enforced ... binary rewards', so its version delta is a scoring-rule change as much as a repair) and on erp-procurement-planning (52 trials; removed, so inside the composition term), and 41 (3.0) / 32 (4.0) trials with reward None (VerifierTimeoutError, RewardFileNotFoundError, CancelledError, AgentSetupTimeoutError). The board accuracies do not reproduce exactly from the trial record under any one rule (3.0 Opus 5/mini-SWE-agent: 42.7 on the board, 42.28 with None = 0, 43.58 excluding None; 4.0 Opus 5 max: 173 reward-1 trials vs 171 'successes'), and the DiD kill clause moves from firing to not firing between None = 0 and None excluded. The counting rule for None and fractional rewards, and for retried trials (4.0 keeps the last of up to 4 attempts, n_attempts up to 4 on 345 trials; 3.0 records retries as separate '__retry-k' trial names with n_attempts = 1), must be pre-registered before any interval is read; E7 cannot compare $V^3_t$ (fractional) with $V^4_t$ (binary) on kv-live-surgery without it.
objections.evidence: dl/all_trials.json (reward and error_type distributions; n_attempts), dl/action_lb3.json, dl/action_lb4.json metrics; record E1, E7
objections.answer: The probe generates its own trials, so the counting rule is pre-registered here rather than inferred from the board: $y = 1$ if and only if the verifier writes reward 1; a trial with no verdict (VerifierTimeoutError, RewardFileNotFoundError, AgentSetupTimeoutError, CancelledError) is $y = 0$ and is logged by end reason; retries are run only on infrastructure errors, never on agent errors, at most two, the last attempt is scored and the retry count is reported per arm; the no-verdict rate per arm is reported, and $\bar\Delta_U$ is given with and without no-verdict trials as the record already said for wall-clock-ended trials. Fractional rewards: verified on dl/all_trials.json, the 4.0 board has none on any task; the 3.0 board has them on kv-live-surgery (6 trials) and erp-procurement-planning (52, removed). For kv-live-surgery the repair is the scoring rule itself, so E7 is not run on it and its $\Delta_t$ is flagged as a scoring-rule change. Conceded with the objection: the free-record verdict flips between None = 0 and None excluded, which is one more reason that reading is 'not resolved'.

objections.persona: systems; checklist: compute-matched / cost lines checked
objections.objection: The GPU line is wrong by a factor of 3 to 6: both revisions carry 3 GPU tasks (jax-speedrun-gpu, fp8-rmsnorm-gemm, math-eval-grader — the last in R, so it has the hybrid cell too), giving 7 cells x 2 models x 3 trials = 42 GPU trials; on the 4.0 board those tasks' trials average 2.99 h (median 1.53 h, p90 7.7 h under the 8-hour timeout), so the probe needs 64 to 126 GPU-hours against the record's '0 to 20' ceiling (still under one GPU-week, so Gate 1 survives, but the budget line and the 'cost_gpu_hours: 20' field are false). The sandbox line is low by about 3x: 1,689-1,995 s per trial is Gemini-Flash-under-mini-SWE-agent; the record's model A, GLM-5.3-Flash, averaged 6,210 s per trial under Claude Code with 14 trials over 7 hours, so 954 trials cost about 1,650 sandbox-hours, not 450-530; weaker open-weight models run to the 8-hour cap more often (Qwen3.8-Max: 38 trials over 7 h, mean 9,953 s).
objections.evidence: dl/all_trials.json durations per row and per GPU task; dl/tasks/*.task.toml gpus fields; record killing_experiment.design and cost_gpu_hours
objections.answer: conceded: verified on dl/all_trials.json (started/finished fields): 4.0-board trials on the three GPU tasks average 2.99 h (n = 525; median 1.53, p90 7.73), 4.61 h for GLM-5.3-Flash under Claude Code; 7 GPU cells x 2 models x 3 trials = 42 trials gives 64 to 126 GPU-hours (194 at GLM-5.3-Flash's own rate), not 'cost_gpu_hours: 20'. GLM-5.3-Flash's mean trial is 6,210 s under Claude Code against the 1,689-1,995 s the record took from the Gemini-Flash mini-SWE-agent rows, so 954 trials are about 1,650 sandbox-hours, priced at step 0. Under one GPU-week (168 h) at the median and over it at GLM-5.3-Flash's own rate, so the surviving probe caps GPU trials at $k = 3$ on the three GPU tasks and reports them as their own stratum. Gate 1's dollar line is unchanged (API spend); the cost fields are rewritten.

objections.persona: theory; checklist:2026-10-20 (each pre-registered outcome informative; equivalence bound)
objections.objection: E7's verifier-only re-grade has no sample: by file paths the only repaired task whose diff touches tests/ alone is pretrain-shard-corruption ($n = 1$; ctr-optimization and freight-dispatch-shift join only if compose image-pinning is discounted, $n \le 3$); 'for $t \in R_V$ the difference $\delta^{\ast}_t - \Delta^{\mathrm{ver}}_t$ is expected to sit inside run noise, which checks the arm' cannot check anything on one task with 6 trials per version. The kill report's redesign note (3) and the record's E7 should be dropped or re-scoped to the 11 tasks whose diff touches tests/ at all, with the instruction/environment channels declared confounded for them.
objections.evidence: dl/sets.json file_changes; dl/task_crawl.json; record E7 and kill report section 9 note (3)
objections.answer: conceded: by file paths the verifier-only set is pretrain-shard-corruption alone (instruction identical after the budget sentence, changes in instruction.md and tests/ only; dl/sets.json and dl/instr_summary.json), $n = 1$; ctr-optimization and freight-dispatch-shift join only if compose image-pinning is discounted. One task with 6 trials per version checks nothing. E7 is re-scoped: both verifiers run on every $(4,4)$ trial of the 11 repaired tasks whose diff touches tests/, reported as a per-task channel table ($\Delta^{\mathrm{ver}}_t$ beside $\delta^{\ast}_t$) with the instruction and environment channels declared confounded, and the sentence 'which checks the arm' is dropped from the record and from the kill report's redesign note (3).

objections.persona: theory; checklist: parallel trends / what the identity assumes
objections.objection: The DiD's parallel-trends assumption is violated in a direction the free record shows is not uniform: the recalibration removed timeouts (3.0 AgentTimeoutError share 5.1% on R and 4.3% on U; 4.0: 0.4% and 0.9%), and $\bar\Delta_U$ by entry runs from $-0.038$ (Grok 4.6, whose timeouts on U fell 17 to 0 while its accuracy fell 6 points) to $+0.072$ (GPT-5.6 Luna). The record's hybrid arm is the right answer to this for the pinned-harness run, but the lab-position verdict ('a lab holding both-version logs computes $\delta$ and $\hat\pi_{\mathrm{DiD}}$ in a day') and the belief-changing outcome (c) both read a DiD that, on the only data such a lab has, is biased by $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$ with an unknown sign per entry; the lab verdict must be downgraded to 'computes a biased $\delta$ in a day'.
objections.evidence: dl/all_trials.json error_type shares by board and set; sim/real_did_out.txt wall-clock-ended counts per entry; record E4, verdict_by_position.lab
objections.answer: conceded: the free record shows the recalibration is not uniform across entries ($\bar\Delta_U$ from $-0.038$ for Grok 4.6, whose timeouts on U fell 17 to 0 while its accuracy fell 6 points, to $+0.072$ for GPT-5.6 Luna; AgentTimeoutError shares fell from 5.1% / 4.3% on R / U in 3.0 to 0.4% / 0.9% in 4.0), so a DiD computed from both-version logs alone is biased by $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$ with a sign that differs by entry. The lab-position verdict is rewritten to 'computes a DiD biased by $\gamma_R - \bar\Delta_U$, of unknown sign, in a day; $\delta^{\ast}$ needs the hybrid arm (about 84 re-run trials on the 14 substantive tasks)'. The probe's hybrid arm is unchanged, and belief-changing outcome (c) stands as the measurement of exactly this bias.

objections.persona: theory; checklist: regime stated, results by band; selection on the baseline
objections.objection: The 19 repaired tasks are a selected set: 6 of them were board-wide all-fail on the 3.0 board (against 5 of 47 U tasks), their 3.0 mean rate was 0.158 vs 0.238 on U, and in 4.0 the two sets sit at 0.411 vs 0.400. Any comparison that uses the 3.0 trials the owners selected on (the free record; a lab's own 3.0 logs if the owners used them; the owners' own 5.0 protocol) carries regression to the mean on $\bar\Delta_R$. The probe's fresh (3,3) re-run avoids it, which is an argument for the re-run the record does not make and should; and the 'established' reading on the free record (objection 2) is an upper bound for that reason.
objections.evidence: dl/all_trials.json board-wide 3.0 and 4.0 per-task rates (all-fail lists); 2609.26826 (the 3.0 production record was screened for all-fail tasks; abstract in the kill report)
objections.answer: Agreed and adopted as the record's stated reason for the fresh $(3,3)$ arm: the 19 repaired tasks were selected on the 3.0 production record (6 of 19 board-wide all-fail on 3.0 against 5 of 47 on U; 3.0 mean rate 0.158 against 0.238), so any $\bar\Delta_R$ that uses the owners' 3.0 trials carries regression to the mean upward, and the free-record 'established' readings in my answer to objection 2 are upper bounds for that reason. A fresh $(3,3)$ arm under the pinned harness is not selected on, which is the one thing the free record cannot supply and the probe can; the record's why_now and the lab-position clause both gain this sentence.

objections.persona: checklist:2026-10-25 (quotes and facts grep-verified before they enter a record); checklist:2026-11-01 (the preserved asset is the package, not the board)
objections.objection: Two facts in the record and one checklist lesson are false on the Hub and must be corrected before the record is read by anyone: 'the 3.0 board is gone (the tbench.ai 3.0 URL serves the 4.0 payload); the preserved asset is the package' (red_team_preanswers) — the tbench.ai URL does serve 4.0, but Harbor Hub revision 1 registers leaderboard 3-0-0 'Terminal-Bench 3.0' with 12 displayed rows; 'Harbor Hub job pages: client-rendered; not opened this session' (degraded) — the pages are client-rendered, and their data is reachable by POSTing the server-action ids in the page's own JS; and the checklist's 2026-11-01 line 'Harbor Hub registers one Terminal-Bench leaderboard (4-0-0) ... a retired version's board disappears while its dataset revision persists' is wrong for the Hub. The lesson to replace it: a Next.js hub's 'loading...' page is not the data; read the chunk for createServerReference ids before writing 'not exposed'.
objections.evidence: dl/rsc_rev1.txt ('leaderboards':[{... 'name':'3-0-0','title':'Terminal-Bench 3.0' ...}]); dl/action_lb3.json; dl/js/*.js; prompts/checklist.md 2026-11-01 entry
objections.answer: conceded: verified in dl/rsc_rev1.txt ('name':'3-0-0', 'title':'Terminal-Bench 3.0', 'The official leaderboard for Terminal-Bench 3.0') and dl/action_lb3.json (12 rows). The record's red_team_preanswers line ('the 3.0 board is gone; the preserved asset is the package'), its degraded entry on job pages, the kill report's section 5 sentence and the checklist's 2026-11-01 line are false for the Hub (true only of tbench.ai) and are corrected; the replacement lesson — a Next.js hub's loading page is not the data; read the chunk for the server-action ids before writing 'not exposed' — is accepted for prompts/checklist.md.

objections.persona: systems; checklist: 'free' part free on the deployed engine; runnable benchmark confirmed
objections.objection: Data gate item (2) ('the pinned harness executes the 3.0.0 revision under the current Harbor CLI') is still untested and is now the only part of step 0 that is not done; the 3.0.0 package builds every environment and sidecar from Dockerfiles at run time (no digests), so the (3,3) arm today is not the (3,3) the 3.0 board ran in July-August 2026 (base images, apt and pip resolutions have moved), while the (4,4) arm pulls digests. Either the (3,3) arm is rebuilt and the image drift accepted as part of $\bar\Delta_U$ (then state it and its 0.83% floor), or the probe needs the 3.0-era images, which the Hub does not pin. Record which before costing.
objections.evidence: dl/tasks/*.3.task.toml (no docker_image on 3.0.0 environments), dl/envf/*.3.compose.yaml ('build: context: ...'); 2610.14460 abstract (kill report)
objections.answer: Recorded before costing, as asked, and it does not break the design. The $(3,3)$ and $(3,4)$ arms are built from the same 3.0.0 Dockerfiles in the same window, so whatever base-image, apt and pip drift has accumulated since July enters both arms alike and $\gamma_R = (3,4) - (3,3)$ carries none of it. The drift enters $\bar\Delta_U$ (rebuilt 3.0 against pinned 4.0 on the untouched tasks) and $\delta^{\ast}$ on the environment-repaired tasks (objection 4), each bounded by 2610.14460's 0.83% of three-run majority verdicts under rebuilt images; $\bar\Delta_U$ is therefore stated as recalibration bundle plus rebuilt-image drift plus harness-era drift, with the free record's $\bar\Delta_U$ (+0.016 pooled, +0.009 in band) as the external reference it is checked against. The $(3,3)$ arm is not the July 3.0 run and the record says so; the probe needs the 3.0.0 package as shipped, not the 3.0-era images.

objections.persona: theory; checklist: pairs share policies, curves share tasks
objections.objection: E9's unit of replication is the board entry, but 35 entries are 23 (agent, model) pairs, of which Fable 5.1 contributes 5 effort rows and GPT-6 Astra 5 and Opus 5 5; the matched null draws subsets of tasks and keeps the 35 correlated rows, so the ceiling is not inflated by the dependence, but the percentile statement ('37th percentile') treats 35 rows as 35 orderings. The record's secondary (one row per model) is the primary; at 23 rows $\rho_{RU} = 0.930$ against 0.882, and the result is unchanged. Re-label the primary.
objections.evidence: dl/action_lb4.json metadata (reasoning_effort rows per model); sim/real_did_out.txt secondary line; record E9 last sentence
objections.answer: Accepted: the primary ordering test is one row per (agent, model), the highest-effort row, 23 rows; the 35-row version is the secondary. The result is the same under both (0.930 against 0.882; 0.902 against 0.839), so the relabel changes the record, not the verdict on clause 2.

objections.persona: professor; checklist: scorecard (register and what it is not; consumers)
objections.objection: With clause 2 dead and clause 1 at $\delta \approx 0.07$ on the free record, the surviving content is the owners' sentence with an interval ('TB 4.0 has fewer agent timeouts and errors than 3.0, reducing measurement noise': timeouts fell from about 4.5% to under 1% of trials, $\bar\Delta_U \approx +0.016$) plus a kept-task delta of about 4 points of which the 19 repaired tasks carry roughly half at the point estimate and anything from nothing to all of it in the interval. That is the floor scenario of the scorecard (p 0.55), reachable at $0 from the Hub today; the middle and ceiling (an owner community ships a repair delta per release) need the kill-search's 'both clauses move a stated belief' and clause 2 no longer does. Re-grade the claim: proper at most for the first clause only, parked for the ordering clause with the trigger 'a second version pair (4.0 to 4.1 verifier fixes, or 5.0) whose repaired subset clears the matched ceiling'.
objections.evidence: sim/real_did_out.txt; dl/all_trials.json error shares; release note (dl pages tb40.html); record scorecard.impact_ceiling
objections.answer: conceded in substance: the ordering clause is dead on this pair, and a pre-registered kill that fired on real data is a kill, not a park — a second version pair (4.0 to 4.1, 5.0) is a new claim, not a re-open trigger for this one. The surviving content is the first clause alone, proper at most. One correction to the objection's own floor reading: 'roughly half at the point estimate and anything from nothing to all of it' is the 7-entry pool with the two floor entries in; in the band the record pre-registered the share's point estimate is 0.7 to 0.9 with the DiD's lower end above zero at one cut, so the first clause is live, not at the floor. The scorecard's middle scenario (an owner ships a repair delta per release) requires the first clause's number, not the ordering clause, so it survives at a lower probability; the ceiling, which needed both clauses on two owners, drops.

objections.persona: theory; checklist: composition term sign (premise numbers with denominators)
objections.objection: The pre-registered 'expected' says 'the composition term positive (the two saturated tasks removed were passes)'; under E6's definition $\Delta_{\mathrm{comp}} = \frac{n_X}{n}(\bar p^{(3,3)}_{\mathrm{kept}} - \bar p^{(3,3)}_X)$ it is negative when the removed tasks were easier, and on the 3.0 board they were (removed mean 0.334 vs kept 0.211 board-wide; per matched entry $-0.011$ to $-0.019$). Fix the sign in the expected outcome, and note that 3 of the 8 removed tasks sit in the all-fail or None-heavy tail (cli-2ph-simplex 9 None-reward trials, lean-midpoint-proof 6, ico-path-patch all-fail), so the composition term is itself partly a counting-rule choice (objection 9).
objections.evidence: sim/real_did_out.txt comp values; dl/all_trials.json removed-task rates; record E6 and preregistered_surprise.expected
objections.answer: conceded: verified on sim/real_did_out.txt — the composition term is $-0.011$ to $-0.019$ per matched entry because the removed tasks were easier than the kept ones on the 3.0 board (0.334 against 0.211), so under E6 it is negative; the expected outcome's sign is corrected, and the dependence of the term on the counting rule for the None-heavy removed tasks (cli-2ph-simplex, lean-midpoint-proof, ico-path-patch) is noted beside it.

objections.persona: systems; checklist: regime stated (model size, pass-rate band)
objections.objection: Model A (GLM-5.3-Flash, 35.8% under Claude Code) will not be a 35% model under mini-SWE-agent: on the 4.0 board the two mini-SWE-agent rows are the two weakest entries (Gemini 3.8 Flash 19.1%, Gemini 3.7 Flash 11.2%) and on the 3.0 board mini-SWE-agent/Opus 5 (42.7%) sat 9 points above Claude Code/Fable 5; the harness moves the band by 10-20 points in either direction. A model in the 10-20% band has most tasks all-fail on both versions, where E3's $\delta^{\ast}$ cannot move (the record's own 'saturated and all-fail strata reported separately because they cannot move'); the budget rule picks the cheapest model B, which is the weakest. Pre-register the band under the pinned harness (a 20-trial pilot on the 4.0 revision, about $20) before the model pair is fixed, and drop any model whose 4.0 all-fail share on R exceeds half.
objections.evidence: dl/action_lb4.json and dl/action_lb3.json rows for mini-SWE-agent; record killing_experiment.design model rule
objections.answer: Adopted as the operational form of the band quantifier (objection 3). Verified: the two mini-SWE-agent rows on the 4.0 board are the two weakest entries (Gemini 3.8 Flash 19.1%, Gemini 3.7 Flash 11.2%) and mini-SWE-agent/Opus 5 sat at 42.7% on 3.0, so the harness moves the band by 10 to 20 points and GLM-5.3-Flash's 35.8% under Claude Code says nothing about its band under mini-SWE-agent. The surviving probe adds a pilot before the model pair is fixed: 20 trials per candidate model on the 4.0 revision under the pinned harness (about $20 each at the board's token rates), with the rule that a model whose 4.0 all-fail share on the 14 substantive repaired tasks exceeds one half is dropped; the free record shows why (GPT-5.6 Luna: 12 of 19 all-fail, $\bar\Delta_R$ = 0.000). The budget rule 'cheapest model B' is subordinated to the band rule.

objections.persona: checklist:2026-10-20 (a claim's headline must be the sentence its cheapest probe tests; one quantifier per sentence)
objections.objection: The claim record's headline (version 3) still carries the DiD share $> 0.5$ and the ordering clause as one conjunction, while the probe asks the claims stage to carry '$\delta^{\ast} > 0.15$ with the share beside it' and treats the kill as a disjunction; the kill report's section 8 says 'AND'. Three documents, three kills. Until the claim record is rewritten, the gate verdict is undefined; and after objection 1 the only surviving sentence is the first clause alone, which must be re-filed as its own claim with the ordering clause parked.
